rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary signals the instruction; treating it as spoken words would contradict her vow not to speak to any human that day.
rows.anchor: المراد بهذا القول: الإشارة إليه بذلك.

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas explains the vowed fast as silence; Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak agree.
rows.anchor: قال أنس بن مالك في قوله: {إني نذرت للرحمن صوما} أي: صمتا

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Another report from Anas combines fasting and silence; Qatada and others agree.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عن أنس: "صوما وصمتا"، وكذا قال قتادة

rows.speaker: السدي، قتادة، عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: In their religious law, fasting prohibited both food and speech.
rows.anchor: والمراد أنهم كانوا إذا صاموا في شريعتهم يحرم عليهم الطعام والكلام

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud told a man who had sworn not to speak to talk and greet people; Mary's silence gave her an excuse because no one would believe an unmarried woman had conceived.
rows.anchor: فقال عبد الله بن مسعود: كلم الناس وسلم عليهم

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd depicts Mary fearing people's suspicion and Jesus telling her he would answer for her and instructing her to signal a vow of silence.
rows.anchor: قال لها عيسى: أنا أكفيك الكلام: {فإما ترين من البشر أحدا فقولي

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد، وهب
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the instruction is all Jesus' speech to his mother; Wahb agrees.
rows.anchor: قال: هذا كله من كلام عيسى لأمه. وكذا قال وهب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary submits to God's command, takes the child to her people, and they react with shock and suspicion.
rows.anchor: فسلمت لأمر الله، عز وجل، واستسلمت لقضائه

rows.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة، السدي
rows.claim: They explain the accusation as saying Mary brought a tremendous matter.
rows.anchor: أي: أمرا عظيما. قاله مجاهد، وقتادة والسدي

rows.speaker: نوف البكالي
rows.claim: Nauf relates that Mary's people searched for her; a herdsman saw his cattle prostrating toward the valley and directed them to her, with a report of a shining light also preserved.
rows.anchor: عن نوف البكالي قال: وخرج قومها في طلبها، وكانت من أهل بيت نبوة وشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call Mary a counterpart to Aaron in worship and ask how someone from a pure, devout family could do this.
rows.anchor: أي: يا شبيهة هارون في العبادة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة، السدي
rows.claim: They report that Mary was called Aaron's sister because she descended from Aaron, Moses' brother, as tribal affiliation can be expressed as brotherhood.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة (2) ، والسدي: قيل لها: {يا أخت هارون} أي: أخي موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that Mary was compared in worship and asceticism to a righteous man named Aaron among her people.
rows.anchor: نسبت إلى رجل صالح كان فيهم اسمه هارون

rows.speaker: بعضهم، سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: A view reported by Ibn Jarir and from Said ibn Jubayr says she was compared with a wicked man named Aaron.
rows.anchor: يقال له: هارون. ورواه ابن أبي حاتم عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Al-Qurazi gives the unusual view that Mary was the full sister of Aaron and of Moses' Aaron, who once tracked Moses.
rows.anchor: عن القرظي في قول الله عز وجل: {يا أخت هارون} قال: هي أخت هارون لأبيه وأمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects al-Qurazi's identification as wholly mistaken: Jesus was the last prophet before Muhammad, so Mary cannot be Moses' sister.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول خطأ محض، فإن الله تعالى قد ذكر في كتابه أنه قفى بعيسى بعد الرسل

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة، النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said he is the closest of people to Jesus, with no prophet between them.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، عن النبي (7) صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "أنا أولى الناس بابن مريم؛ إلا أنه (8) ليس بيني وبينه نبي"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If al-Qurazi's claim were true, Jesus would precede David and Solomon, although the Quran places David after Moses.
rows.anchor: ولكان قبل سليمان و (9) داود؛ فإن الله قد ذكر أن داود بعد موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurazi was misled by the Torah's account of Miriam, Moses' and Aaron's sister; she merely shared the name Mary, as people were named for prophets and righteous figures.
rows.anchor: وهي (10) هفوة وغلطة شديدة، بل هي باسم هذه

rows.speaker: المغيرة بن شعبة، النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When Christians at Najran questioned the chronology of calling Mary Aaron's sister, the Prophet said earlier people used prophets' and righteous people's names.
rows.anchor: عن المغيرة بن شعبة قال: بعثني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى نجران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report is found in Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasai; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih gharib and says it is known only through Ibn Idris.
rows.anchor: وقال الترمذي: حسن صحيح غريب، لا نعرفه إلا من حديث ابن إدريس

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka'b says Aaron in the address was not Moses' brother; Aisha challenges him, saying he is wrong unless the Prophet said it, while noting a six-hundred-year gap.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين قال نبئت أن كعبا قال: إن قوله: {يا أخت هارون} : ليس بهارون أخي موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the chronology cited in this report is open to question.
rows.anchor: قال: فسكتت (4) وفي هذا التاريخ نظر.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Mary came from a household known for righteousness, while families can become known for righteousness or corruption across generations.
rows.anchor: قال: كانت من أهل بيت يعرفون بالصلاح، ولا يعرفون بالفساد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says this was a different reformer Aaron, beloved among his people, and reports that forty thousand named Aaron attended his funeral.
rows.anchor: وكان هارون مصلحا محببا، في عشيرته، وليس بهارون أخي (6) موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary had been fasting and silent, so she redirected her accusers to the child, whom they thought she was mockingly asking them to address.
rows.anchor: وقد كانت يومها ذلك صائمة، صامتة فأحالت الكلام عليه

rows.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
rows.claim: Maymun says Mary pointed to Jesus and told the people to speak to him; they protest at being asked to question an infant after such an accusation.
rows.anchor: قال ميمون بن مهران: {فأشارت [إليه] } (8) ، قالت: كلموه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the people were angered and considered her apparent mockery worse than the alleged adultery.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: لما أشارت إليه غضبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase describes someone actually present in a cradle during infancy and early childhood, so the crowd asks how he could speak.
rows.anchor: أي: من هو موجود في مهده في حال صباه وصغره، كيف يتكلم؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus first declares himself God's servant, thereby glorifying God beyond having a child and affirming his own servitude.
rows.anchor: أول شيء تكلم به أن نزه جناب ربه تعالى (10) وبرأ الله عن الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' declaration that he received scripture and prophethood clears his mother of the accusation of sexual misconduct.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {آتاني الكتاب وجعلني نبيا} : تبرئة لأمه مما نسبت إليه من الفاحشة

rows.speaker: نوف البكالي
rows.claim: Nauf says Jesus was nursing when people accused his mother; he withdrew from the breast, leaned on his left side, and spoke through the declaration of lifelong prayer and almsgiving.
rows.anchor: قال نوف البكالي: لما قالوا لأمه ما قالوا، كان يرتضع ثديه

rows.speaker: ثابت البناني
rows.claim: Thabit reports that Jesus raised his index finger above his shoulder while saying he was God's servant, given scripture and made a prophet.
rows.anchor: عن ثابت البناني: رفع إصبعه السبابة فوق منكبه

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima interprets receiving the Book as God's decree that Jesus would receive it.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: {آتاني الكتاب} أي: قضى أنه (1) يؤتيني الكتاب

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas is reported to say that Jesus learned and mastered the Gospel in his mother's womb; Ibn Kathir says Yahya ibn Said al-Attar is abandoned in hadith.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، رضي الله عنه، قال: كان عيسى ابن مريم قد درس الإنجيل وأحكمه (3) في بطن أمه

rows.speaker: مجاهد، عمرو بن قيس، الثوري
rows.claim: They explain Jesus' being blessed wherever he is as teaching good; another report from Mujahid says he is beneficial to others.
rows.anchor: وجعلني معلما للخير. وفي رواية عن مجاهد: نفاعا.

rows.speaker: وهيب بن الورد
rows.claim: A scholar says the most public deed is commanding right and forbidding wrong, the religion God sent through the prophets; jurists agreed this is Jesus' blessing wherever he is.
rows.anchor: الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر؛ فإنه دين الله الذي بعث به أنبياءه إلى عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' charge to pray and give alms for life parallels God's command to Muhammad to worship until death, called certainty.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم: {واعبد ربك حتى يأتيك اليقين}

rows.speaker: مالك بن أنس
rows.claim: Malik says Jesus was informed of what would happen to him until death, a point against the Qadariyya.
rows.anchor: عن مالك بن أنس في قوله: {وأوصاني بالصلاة والزكاة ما دمت حيا} قال: أخبره بما هو كائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' dutifulness to his mother is mentioned after obedience to God because scripture often pairs worship of God with kindness to parents.
rows.anchor: لأن الله تعالى كثيرا ما يقرن (6) بين الأمر بعبادته وطاعة الوالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not being a tyrant or wretched means Jesus was not arrogant about worship, obedience, or kindness to his mother and thus did not make himself wretched.
rows.anchor: ولم يجعلني جبارا مستكبرا عن عبادته وطاعته وبر والدتي

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Al-Thawri defines a tyrannical wretch as one who readily turns to anger.
rows.anchor: قال سفيان الثوري: الجبار الشقي: الذي يقبل (7) على الغضب.

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: Some early authorities say everyone who mistreats parents is tyrannical and wretched; they link bad treatment of dependents with conceit, citing the command about those under one's care.
rows.anchor: لا تجد أحدا عاقا لوالديه إلا وجدته جبارا شقيا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: After a woman praised Jesus' mother and nurse while seeing his miracles, Jesus said blessed are those who read and follow God's speech without becoming tyrannical and wretched.
rows.anchor: فقال نبي الله عيسى، عليه السلام، يجيبها: طوبى لمن تلا كلام (1) الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' greeting of peace at birth, death, and resurrection affirms that he is God's created servant who lives, dies, and is raised like other creatures, while protected in these hardest moments.
rows.anchor: وأنه مخلوق من خلق الله يحيا (2) ويموت ويبعث كسائر الخلائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Muhammad that the account of Jesus is the true statement over which proponents of falsehood and truth differ.
rows.anchor: أي: يختلف المبطلون والمحقون ممن آمن به وكفر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use the nominative qawl al-haqq; Asim and Abdullah ibn Amir read the phrase with a different case, while Ibn Masud reads it as qāla al-haqq.
rows.anchor: قرأ الأكثرون: "قول الحق" برفع قول. وقرأ عاصم، وعبد الله بن عامر: {قول الحق}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative reading has the clearest grammar and is supported by the statement that truth is from the Lord.
rows.anchor: والرفع أظهر إعرابا، ويشهد له قوله تعالى: {الحق من ربك فلا تكن من الممترين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After identifying Jesus as a servant and prophet, God declares Himself far above the claim of a son; when God wills something, He commands it and it comes to be.
rows.anchor: أي: إذا أراد شيئا فإنما يأمر به، فيصير (5) كما يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus told his people in the cradle that God is his Lord and theirs and commanded worship; the straight path is upright, guiding its followers and leading its opponents astray.
rows.anchor: أي: قويم، من اتبعه رشد وهدى، ومن خالفه ضل وغوى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Jesus' status was made clear, the People of the Book split into factions; Ibn Kathir endorses that he is God's servant and messenger, word cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him.
rows.anchor: وأنه عبده (2) ورسوله وكلمته ألقاها إلى مريم وروح منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority of Jews called Jesus illegitimate and his speech magic; others said God spoke, he was God's son, one of three, or God's servant and messenger, the true view.
rows.anchor: فصممت طائفة -وهم جمهور اليهود، عليهم لعائن الله -على أنه ولد زنية، وقالوا: كلامه هذا سحر.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada describes four Israelite representatives disputing Jesus: one group said he was God descended to earth, another God's son, another one of three, and the fourth God's servant, messenger, spirit, and word; they acquired followers and fought.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {ذلك عيسى ابن مريم قول الحق الذي فيه يمترون} ، قال: اجتمع بنو إسرائيل

rows.speaker: عمرو بن ميمون، ابن جريج، قتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says a similar account of the factions is transmitted from these early authorities and others.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن ميمون، وابن جريج، وقتادة، وغير واحد من السلف والخلف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، عروة بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits a similar account of disagreement over Jesus from Ibn Abbas, Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, and other scholars.
rows.anchor: وقد روى ابن أبي حاتم، عن ابن عباس، وعن عروة بن الزبير، وعن بعض أهل العلم، قريبا من ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Historians report that Constantine convened a council of 2,170 bishops who expressed many competing positions on Jesus, with only 308 agreeing on one doctrine.
rows.anchor: فكان جماعة الأساقفة (12) منهم ألفين ومائة وسبعين أسقفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the king favored the 308, expelled opponents, and they devised a creed, laws, and innovations that changed Christianity; Constantine built many churches and Helena built the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, while Jesus had been raised rather than crucified.
rows.anchor: فقدمهم ونصرهم وطرد من عداهم، فوضعوا له الأمانة الكبيرة، بل هي الخيانة العظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning threatens those who lie about God and claim He has a son; God delays punishment though fully able to seize wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: تهديد ووعيد شديد لمن كذب على الله، وافترى، وزعم أن له ولدا.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says God gives a wrongdoer respite and, once seized, does not let him escape.
rows.anchor: إن الله ليملي (4) للظالم حتى إذا أخذه لم يفلته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says no one is more patient than God with hurtful claims that He has a child, even while He continues to provide and heal their claimants.
rows.anchor: لا أحد أصبر على أذى سمعه (5) من الله، إنهم يجعلون له ولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great day on which disbelievers face their fate is the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال هاهنا: {فويل للذين كفروا من مشهد يوم عظيم} أي: يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت، النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet promises Paradise to whoever testifies to God's oneness, Muhammad's messengership, Jesus' servitude, messengership, word and spirit, and the truth of Paradise and Hell, whatever their deeds.
rows.anchor: وأن عيسى عبد الله [ورسوله] (7) وكلمته ألقاها إلى مريم وروح منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day disbelievers will hear and see fully, as those asking to return after seeing punishment; then it is too late, whereas certainty before seeing it could have saved them.
rows.anchor: أي: يقولون ذلك حين لا ينفعهم ولا يجدي (2) عنهم شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording marvels at their hearing and sight when they come to God; in worldly life they neither hear, see, nor reason toward guidance, obeying only when it will not help.
rows.anchor: أي: ما أسمعهم وأبصرهم {يوم يأتوننا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Regret is when judgment separates the people of Paradise and Hell, each entering an everlasting destination; people now remain heedless and do not believe.
rows.anchor: فصل بين أهل الجنة وأهل النار، ودخل كل إلى ما صار إليه مخلدا فيه

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري، النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Death will be presented as a ram between Paradise and Hell and slaughtered, after which each group is told it will remain forever; Ibn Kathir says Bukhari and Muslim narrate it with similar wording.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد [الخدري] (1) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا دخل أهل الجنة الجنة، وأهل النار النار، يجاء بالموت كأنه كبش أملح

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة، النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A parallel report about the slaughtering of death is transmitted from Abu Hurayra through al-A'mash and through Muhammad ibn Amr in Ibn Majah.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة مرفوعا، مثله. وفي سنن ابن ماجه وغيره، من حديث محمد بن عمرو

rows.speaker: ابن عمر، النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the report about death being slaughtered is also found in the Sahihayn from Ibn Umar.
rows.anchor: وهو في الصحيحين عن ابن عمر (7)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj transmits a similar account from Ibn Abbas and reports that Ubayd ibn Umayr described death as an animal brought and slaughtered while people watched.
rows.anchor: ورواه ابن جريج قال: قال ابن عباس: فذكر من قبله نحوه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says everyone sees a home in Paradise and one in Hell; Hell's people regret the Paradise home they could have had through faith and good works, while Paradise's people see their alternative home in Hell.
rows.anchor: قال: فليس نفس إلا وهي تنظر إلى بيت في الجنة وبيت في النار، وهو يوم الحسرة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud describes death as a ram all inhabitants of the highest Paradise and lowest Hell see before it is slaughtered and both groups are told they will remain forever; their joy and grief would kill them if death were possible.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله: {وأنذرهم يوم الحسرة إذ قضي الأمر} قال: إذا دخل أهل الجنة الجنة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: The report explains that the settlement of the matter occurs when death is slaughtered.
rows.anchor: يقول: إذا ذبح الموت. رواه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Day of Regret is one of the names of the Resurrection, magnified by God as a warning to His servants.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وأنذرهم يوم الحسرة} من أسماء يوم القيامة عظمه الله

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies it as the Resurrection and links it to the soul's regret over neglecting God's cause.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم في قوله: {وأنذرهم يوم الحسرة} قال: يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone creates, owns, and governs; all creatures die while He remains their heir and judge, and no one will suffer even the slightest injustice.
rows.anchor: وأن الخلق كلهم يهلكون ويبقى هو، تعالى وتقدس ولا أحد يدعي ملكا ولا تصرفا

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz writes that God decreed death for creation, made their return to Him, and revealed that He inherits the earth and its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: كتب عمر بن عبد العزيز إلى عبد الحميد بن عبد الرحمن صاحب الكوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to recount Abraham to idol-worshipping people who claim his religious way; Abraham was a truthful prophet and gently challenged his father about powerless idols.
rows.anchor: واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم واتله على قومك، هؤلاء الذين يعبدون الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot hear, see, benefit their worshippers, or protect them from harm.
rows.anchor: أي: لا ينفعك ولا يدفع عنك ضررا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though Abraham was his father's child and younger, God gave him knowledge his father had not received; he offers to guide him on a straight path to benefit and safety.
rows.anchor: فاعلم أني قد اطلعت من العلم من الله على ما لم تعلمه أنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping Satan means obeying him by worshipping idols, since Satan calls people to this and approves it; Quranic parallels warn against worshipping Satan and say idolaters invoke a rebellious Satan.
rows.anchor: أي: لا تطعه (1) في عبادتك هذه الأصنام، فإنه هو الداعي إلى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is rebellious and arrogant against the Merciful, so God expelled him; following him would make Abraham like Satan.
rows.anchor: فطرده وأبعده، فلا تتبعه تصر مثله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham fears punishment for his father's idolatry and disobedience; Satan's ally has no patron, helper, or rescuer, and following Satan brings punishment.
rows.anchor: يعني: فلا يكون لك مولى ولا ناصرا ولا مغيثا إلا إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's father means that if he will not worship the idols he must stop insulting them; otherwise he threatens retaliation and abuse.
rows.anchor: فانته عن سبها وشتمها وعيبها، فإنك إن لم تنته عن ذلك اقتصصت منك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي، ابن جريج، الضحاك
rows.claim: These authorities explain the father's threat as threatening to stone or revile Abraham.
rows.anchor: وهو (5) قوله: {لأرجمنك} ، قاله ابن عباس، والسدي، وابن جريج

rows.speaker: مجاهد، عكرمة، سعيد بن جبير، محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: They interpret the command to leave for a while as a long time.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد، وعكرمة، وسعيد بن جبير، ومحمد بن إسحاق: يعني دهرا.

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan also interprets the requested separation as a long time.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: زمانا طويلا.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the father meant Abraham should leave forever.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: {واهجرني مليا} قال: أبدا.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, Qatada, Atiyya, and Abu Malik say leave safely before punishment; Ibn Jarir chooses this view.
rows.anchor: سويا سالما، قبل أن تصيبك مني عقوبة. وكذا قال الضحاك، وقتادة وعطية الجدلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's peaceful farewell echoes believers responding peacefully to ignorant people and withdrawing from vain speech.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى في صفة المؤمنين: {وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham assures his father he will not harm him, out of respect for their parent-child bond, and says he will ask God to guide and forgive him.
rows.anchor: أما أنا فلا ينالك مني مكروه ولا أذى، وذلك لحرمة الأبوة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and others explain God's attentiveness to Abraham as gentleness in guiding him to sincere worship.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره: لطيفا، أي: في أن هداني لعبادته والإخلاص له

rows.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and others explain God's attentiveness as His repeated answering of Abraham's prayers.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة، وغيرهما: {إنه كان بي حفيا} قال (1) : [و] (2) عوده الإجابة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the description as God caring about Abraham's affairs.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: "الحفي": الذي يهتم بأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham continued seeking forgiveness for his father after migrating, building the sanctuary, and having children, as in his prayer at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقد استغفر إبراهيم لأبيه مدة طويلة، وبعد أن هاجر إلى الشام وبنى المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Early Muslims sought forgiveness for unbelieving relatives by Abraham's example until revelation clarified the exception and prohibited seeking forgiveness after their fate was known.
rows.anchor: وقد استغفر المسلمون لقراباتهم وأهليهم من المشركين في ابتداء الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham separates from his people, disavows their idols, and worships God alone without partner.
rows.anchor: أي: أجتنبكم وأتبرأ منكم ومن آلهتكم التي تعبدونها [من دون الله] (6)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's hope not to be wretched in supplication is certain to be fulfilled, since he is the greatest prophet after Muhammad.
rows.anchor: و "عسى" هذه موجبة لا محالة، فإنه عليه السلام، سيد الأنبياء بعد محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Abraham separated from his father and people for God's sake, God replaced them with better company and granted him Isaac and Isaac's son Jacob.
rows.anchor: أبدله الله من هو خير منهم، ووهب له إسحاق ويعقوب، يعني ابنه وابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran establishes Isaac as Jacob's father, and Abraham's descendants were prophets, bringing him joy during his lifetime.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف أن إسحاق والد يعقوب، وهو نص القرآن في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob must have become a prophet during Abraham's lifetime, since the passage names Jacob rather than his son Joseph, also a prophet.
rows.anchor: فلو لم يكن يعقوب قد نبئ في حياة إبراهيم، لما اقتصر عليه، ولذكر ولده يوسف

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A sound, agreed-upon report identifies Joseph as a prophet, son of the prophet Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham; another wording calls him the noble son of a noble lineage.
rows.anchor: فقال: "يوسف نبي الله، ابن يعقوب نبي الله، ابن إسحاق نبي الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the elevated true mention granted to Abraham's family as good praise; al-Suddi and Malik agree.
rows.anchor: يعني الثناء الحسن. وكذا قال السدي، ومالك بن أنس.

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says their praise is high because all religious communities commend them.
rows.anchor: لأن جميع الملل والأديان يثنون عليهم ويمدحونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Abraham, the passage turns to Moses, both a messenger and prophet, one of the five great messengers: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: فإنه كان من المرسلين الكبار أولي (5) العزم الخمسة، وهم: نوح وإبراهيم

rows.speaker: عيسى
rows.claim: On the reading with kasra in mukhliṣan, Moses is sincere in worship; Jesus defines sincere work as done for God without wanting people's praise.
rows.anchor: قال: الذي يعمل لله، لا يحب أن يحمده الناس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readers use the fatha form, meaning Moses was chosen, as in God's statement that He selected him above people.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون (4) بفتحها، بمعنى أنه كان مصطفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God called Moses from the mountain's right side, relative to Moses, where he had gone seeking a brand from a fire near the valley's bank, then spoke to and drew him close.
rows.anchor: أي: من جانبه الأيمن من موسى حين ذهب يبتغي من تلك النار جذوة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses was brought so near that he heard the pen scratching as the Torah was written; Mujahid, Abu al-Aliyah, and others agree.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وقربناه نجيا} قال: أدني حتى سمع (10) صريف القلم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Moses was taken into heaven and spoken to there; Mujahid transmits a similar view.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: {وقربناه نجيا} قال: أدخل في السماء فكلم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada gives a different gloss of najiyyan: Moses was saved through his truthfulness.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: {وقربناه نجيا} قال: نجا بصدقه (1)

rows.speaker: عمرو بن معد يكرب
rows.claim: A report says God told Moses that a grateful heart, remembering tongue, and wife who helps in good leave no good withheld; withholding these means good has not been opened to a person.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن معد يكرب قال: لما قرب الله موسى نجيا بطور سيناء، قال: يا موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered Moses' request and intercession by making Aaron a prophet, as other passages show.
rows.anchor: وأجبنا سؤاله وشفاعته في أخيه، فجعلناه نبيا

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: Some early authorities say no one interceded for another in this world more greatly than Moses interceded for Aaron to become a prophet.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال بعض السلف: ما شفع أحد في أحد شفاعة في الدنيا أعظم من شفاعة موسى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Aaron was older than Moses, and that the gift to Moses was Aaron's prophethood.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قوله: {ووهبنا له من رحمتنا أخاه هارون نبيا} ، قال: كان هارون أكبر من موسى، ولكن أراد: وهب له نبوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God praises Ishmael son of Abraham, ancestor of all Arabs of the Hijaz, for keeping his promises.
rows.anchor: وهو والد عرب الحجاز كلهم بأنه {كان صادق الوعد}

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Ishmael never made a commitment to his Lord without fulfilling it, including worship undertaken by vow.
rows.anchor: ابن جريج: لم يعد ربه عدة إلا أنجزها، يعني: ما التزم قط عبادة (5) بنذر

rows.speaker: سهل بن عقيل
rows.claim: A report says Ishmael waited overnight and into the next day at a promised meeting place after the other man forgot, refusing to leave until he came.
rows.anchor: أن سهل بن عقيل حدثه، أن إسماعيل النبي، عليه السلام، وعد رجلا مكانا أن يأتيه

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Al-Thawri says he heard that Ishmael waited at the meeting place for a full year.
rows.anchor: بلغني أنه أقام في ذلك المكان ينتظره حولا حتى جاءه.

rows.speaker: ابن شوذب
rows.claim: Ibn Shawdhab says Ishmael made the promised place his home.
rows.anchor: بلغني أنه اتخذ ذلك الموضع سكنا.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي الحمساء، النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A pre-prophethood acquaintance forgot money owed to Muhammad and returned on the third day, finding him still waiting; Ibn Kathir calls related reports good.
rows.anchor: يا فتى، لقد شققت (4) علي، أنا هاهنا منذ ثلاث أنتظرك

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Ishmael was called truthful in promise because he told his father he would be patient and then fulfilled it.
rows.anchor: لأنه قال لأبيه: {ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصابرين} [الصافات: 102] ، فصدق في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keeping promises is praiseworthy and breaking them blameworthy; Quran and hadith identify failure to fulfill one's words as hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: فصدق الوعد من الصفات الحميدة، كما أن خلفه من الصفات الذميمة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet lists lying when speaking, breaking a promise, and betraying a trust as three signs of hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: "آية المنافق ثلاث: إذا حدث كذب، وإذا وعد أخلف، وإذا اؤتمن خان"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truthful promise-keeping is the opposite of hypocrisy; Muhammad kept every promise and praised Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi for doing so.
rows.anchor: لا يعد أحدا شيئا إلا وفى له به، وقد أثنى على أبي العاص بن الربيع زوج ابنته زينب

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
rows.claim: After Muhammad died, Abu Bakr promised to settle his commitments; Jabir recalled a promise of Bahrain wealth, and Abu Bakr gave him two measures of five hundred dirhams.
rows.anchor: قال الخليفة أبو بكر الصديق: من كان له عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عدة أو دين فليأتني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir takes Ishmael's description as messenger and prophet to distinguish him from Isaac, who is called a prophet only; a report in Sahih Muslim supports the claim.
rows.anchor: لأنه إنما وصف (1) بالنبوة فقط، وإسماعيل وصف (2) بالنبوة والرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael steadfastly obeyed God and instructed his family, as Muhammad was commanded to order his household to pray and believers to protect their families from the Fire through good and forbidding wrong.
rows.anchor: حيث كان مثابرا على طاعة ربه آمرا بها لأهله (5)

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة، النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet invokes mercy on spouses who rise for night prayer and wake each other, even sprinkling water on a reluctant partner; Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah transmit it.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "رحم الله رجلا قام من الليل فصلى، وأيقظ امرأته

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد، أبو هريرة، النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says spouses who wake each other and pray two units at night are recorded among those who remember God often; Abu Dawud, al-Nasai, and Ibn Majah transmit it.
rows.anchor: إذا استيقظ الرجل من الليل وأيقظ امرأته، فصليا ركعتين، كتبا من الذاكرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idris is praised as a truthful prophet whom God raised high; the sound report of the Night Journey places him in the fourth heaven.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مر به في ليلة الإسراء وهو في السماء الرابعة.

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: In an Israelite account, God promised Idris daily merit like all Adam's children; an angel carried him up to seek more deeds, and the Angel of Death took his soul in the fourth heaven, explaining his exaltation.
rows.anchor: هذا من أخبار كعب الأحبار الإسرائيليات، وفي بعضه نكارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the report an Israelite account and says some of it is objectionable, leaving its full assessment to God.
rows.anchor: هذا من أخبار كعب الأحبار الإسرائيليات، وفي بعضه نكارة، والله أعلم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second version has Idris ask how much of his life remained; the Angel of Death says only a moment, then finds Idris already under his wing and takes his soul there.
rows.anchor: إنك تسألني (7) عن رجل ما بقي من عمره إلا طرفة عين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report says Idris was a tailor who said Glory be to God with each stitch and ended every day with the best deeds on earth.
rows.anchor: أن إدريس كان خياطا، فكان (10) لا يغرز إبرة إلا قال: "سبحان الله"

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Idris was raised without dying, as Jesus was raised.
rows.anchor: قال ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد في قوله: {ورفعناه مكانا عليا} قال: إدريس رفع ولم يمت

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Another report from Mujahid says Idris was raised to the fourth heaven.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان، عن منصور، عن مجاهد: {ورفعناه مكانا عليا} قال: [رفع إلى] (12) السماء الرابعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الضحاك بن مزاحم
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak say Idris was raised to the sixth heaven and died there.
rows.anchor: وقال العوفي عن ابن عباس: {ورفعناه مكانا عليا} قال: رفع إلى السماء السادسة فمات بها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and others interpret the high place as Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن، وغيره، في قوله: {ورفعناه مكانا عليا} قال: الجنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage shifts from individual prophets to the whole class; it is not restricted to those named in this surah.
rows.anchor: بل جنس الأنبياء عليهم السلام، استطرد من ذكر الأشخاص إلى الجنس

rows.speaker: السدي، ابن جرير
rows.claim: They map the lineages as Idris from Adam, Abraham among those carried with Noah, Isaac, Jacob, and Ishmael from Abraham, and Moses, Aaron, Zechariah, John, and Jesus from Israel.
rows.anchor: فالذي عنى به من ذرية آدم: إدريس، والذي عنى به من ذرية من حملنا مع نوح: إبراهيم

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says lineages are separated although all descend from Adam because Idris was Noah's grandfather and not descended from those carried in the ark.
rows.anchor: لأن فيهم من ليس من ولد من كان مع نوح في السفينة، وهو إدريس، فإنه جد نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says it is most apparent that Idris was in Noah's direct ancestral line.
rows.anchor: قلت: هذا هو الأظهر أن إدريس في عمود نسب نوح، عليهما السلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When prophets heard God's speech containing proofs and evidences, they prostrated in humility, submission, praise, and gratitude for blessings.
rows.anchor: إذا سمعوا كلام الله المتضمن حججه ودلائله وبراهينه، سجدوا لربهم خضوعا واستكانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buki is the plural of a crying person, and scholars unanimously consider prostration here prescribed in emulation of the prophets.
rows.anchor: "والبكي": جمع باك، فلهذا أجمع العلماء على شرعية السجود هاهنا

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar recited Surat Maryam and prostrated, saying this is the prostration but asking where the weeping was; he meant the crying mentioned in the verse.
rows.anchor: عن أبي معمر قال: قرأ عمر بن الخطاب، رضي الله عنه، سورة مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the blessed prophets and followers who uphold God's commands, fulfill obligations, and avoid prohibitions, later generations neglect prayer, pursue worldly desires, and meet loss at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: من القائمين بحدود الله وأوامره، المؤدين فرائض الله، التاركين لزواجره

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي، ابن زيد بن أسلم، السدي
rows.claim: They interpret wasting prayer as abandoning it completely; Ibn Jarir prefers this view.
rows.anchor: المراد بإضاعتها تركها بالكلية، قاله محمد بن كعب القرظي، وابن زيد بن أسلم، والسدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some early and later scholars, including the famous position of Ahmad and one report from al-Shafii, declared one who abandons prayer an unbeliever based on two hadiths equating abandonment with disbelief.
rows.anchor: ذهب من ذهب من السلف والخلف والأئمة كما هو المشهور عن الإمام أحمد

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي، القاسم بن مخيمرة
rows.claim: They say prayer was wasted by missing its appointed times; if it meant total abandonment, that would be unbelief.
rows.anchor: إنما أضاعوا المواقيت، ولو كان تركا كان كفرا.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud explains repeated Quranic praise of maintaining prayer as keeping its times; leaving it altogether would be unbelief.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: على مواقيتها. قالوا: ما كنا نرى ذلك إلا على الترك؟

rows.speaker: مسروق
rows.claim: Masruq says no one who maintains the five prayers is counted among the heedless, while wasting them past their times brings ruin.
rows.anchor: قال مسروق: لا يحافظ أحد على الصلوات الخمس، فيكتب من الغافلين

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz says later generations did not abandon prayer but wasted its appointed time.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: لم تكن (9) إضاعتهم تركها، ولكن أضاعوا الوقت.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says these successors appear at the end of time after the righteous of Muhammad's community are gone, engaging in sex openly in alleys; Ibn Jurayj transmits the same view.
rows.anchor: عند قيام الساعة، وذهاب صالحي أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، ينزو بعضهم على بعض في الأزقة

rows.speaker: مجاهد، عكرمة، عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: These authorities identify the successors as people of this Muslim community in its last age.
rows.anchor: أنهم من هذه الأمة، يعنون في آخر الزمان.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid describes people of this community heaping upon one another like livestock and donkeys in public, without fear of God or shame before people.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد: {فخلف من بعدهم خلف أضاعوا الصلاة واتبعوا الشهوات} ، قال: هم في هذه الأمة (2) ، يتراكبون

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري، النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report warns that a generation after sixty years will waste prayer and follow desires; later people recite Quran without it passing their throats, and believer, hypocrite, and sinner recite it for different reasons.
rows.anchor: يكون خلف بعد ستين سنة، أضاعوا الصلاة واتبعوا الشهوات، فسوف يلقون غيا.

rows.speaker: الوليد بن قيس
rows.claim: Al-Walid explains that the believer believes the Quran, the hypocrite disbelieves in it, and the sinner uses it to earn a living.
rows.anchor: قال: المؤمن مؤمن به، والمنافق كافر به، والفاجر يأكل به.

rows.speaker: عائشة، النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Aisha said the Prophet identified the people described as successors as Berbers; Ibn Kathir calls this report gharib.
rows.anchor: فإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "هم الخلف الذين قال الله تعالى: {فخلف من بعدهم خلف أضاعوا الصلاة}

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab says the successors are western people who rule and are the worst of rulers.
rows.anchor: عن شيخ من أهل المدينة؛ أنه سمع محمد بن كعب القرظي يقول في قوله (10) : {فخلف من بعدهم خلف} الآية

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka'b says scripture describes hypocrites as habitual drinkers, prayer abandoners, dice players, sleepers through night prayer, late for dawn prayer, and deserters of Friday prayer.
rows.anchor: شرابين للقهوات تراكين (1) للصلوات، لعابين بالكعبات

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says they shut down mosques and devoted themselves to their properties and farms.
rows.anchor: عطلوا المساجد، ولزموا الضيعات.

rows.speaker: أبو الأشهب العطاردي
rows.claim: A divine address to David warns that worldly desires veil attached hearts; the easiest consequence of preferring desire over God is deprivation from obedience.
rows.anchor: وإن أهون ما أصنع بالعبد من عبيدي إذا آثر شهوة من شهواته علي (3) أن أحرمه طاعتي

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر، النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet feared milk leading people to rural life, desires, and abandoned prayers, and Quran studied by hypocrites to dispute with believers; Ibn Kathir notes a parallel route from Ibn Lahia.
rows.anchor: فيتبعون الريف، ويتبعون الشهوات ويتركون الصلوات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the threatened ghayy as loss; Qatada explains it as evil.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {فسوف يلقون غيا} أي: خسرانا. وقال قتادة: شرا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says ghayy is a deep valley in Hell with foul food.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود: {فسوف يلقون غيا} قال: واد في جهنم، بعيد القعر، خبيث الطعم

rows.speaker: أبو عياض
rows.claim: Abu Iyad describes ghayy as a valley in Hell of pus and blood.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عياض في قوله: {فسوف يلقون غيا} قال: واد في جهنم من قيح ودم

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة، النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says a ten-ounce rock thrown from Hell's brink would take fifty years to reach its bottom and then reach Ghayy and Atham, two wells receiving Hell's pus, linking this to the warning about unlawful killing and adultery.
rows.anchor: بئران في أسفل جهنم، يسيل فيهما صديد أهل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the report about Ghayy and Atham rare and its elevation to the Prophet objectionable.
rows.anchor: هذا حديث غريب ورفعه منكر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is for those who repent from abandoning prayer and following desires; God accepts them, improves their outcome, and makes them heirs of Paradise without diminishing their deeds.
rows.anchor: أي: إلا من رجع عن ترك الصلوات واتباع الشهوات، فإن الله يقبل توبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance erases what preceded it, so past deeds do not reduce later reward through God's generosity.
rows.anchor: وذلك؛ لأن التوبة تجب ما قبلها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith says the repentant sinner is like one who has no sin.
rows.anchor: "التائب من الذنب كمن لا ذنب له"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same exception structure appears in the passage about major sins, where repentance and faith lead to good deeds replacing evil deeds.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاستثناء هاهنا كقوله في سورة الفرقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repentant enter gardens of lasting residence, promised by the Merciful to unseen-believing servants whose certainty and faith are strong despite not seeing them.
rows.anchor: أي: هي من الغيب الذي يؤمنون به وما رأوه؛ وذلك لشدة إيقانهم وقوة إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise's being attained emphasizes certainty and stability; God does not fail or alter a promise, as in the parallel description of an inevitable promise.
rows.anchor: فإن الله لا يخلف الميعاد ولا يبدله، كقوله: {كان وعده مفعولا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording may mean the servants will go to the Garden and that it will come to them.
rows.anchor: أي: العباد صائرون إليه، وسيأتونه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the word can mean coming, since Arabic treats reaching someone and their reaching you as equivalent.
rows.anchor: لأن كل ما أتاك فقد أتيته، كما تقول العرب: أتت علي خمسون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Garden contains no idle, empty, or meaningless speech.
rows.anchor: ليس فيها كلام ساقط تافه لا معنى له، كما قد يوجد في الدنيا.
